groups.sentence: Instructors draw on listed AI teaching resources, guidance pages, sample syllabus statements, disclosure examples and assignment repositories.
Instructors review university and school AI guidelines before the course.
Administrators compile and maintain central AI resource portals and tell instructors about them.
Instructors consult syllabus statement guidance and state their AI expectations clearly to students.
Instructors share the listed AI resources and citation guides with students and put them in the syllabus.
Instructors point students to AI literacy guides and student guides to set classroom norms.
Instructors link their course AI policy to the academic honesty policy or honor code and campus AI guidance.
Students consult the library and style-guide pages on citing and disclosing generative AI in APA, MLA and Chicago formats.
Everyone uses library databases and approved AI tools and data allowances.
Everyone is pointed to academic integrity and misconduct policies, processes and support resources.
Instructors consult the conduct or academic integrity office when AI misuse is suspected.
Everyone consults institutional AI policies, hubs and guidance pages and reviews the university's AI guidelines.
Students are pointed to student guides and library pages on AI and review the named AI guidelines before using AI.
Everyone is pointed to data classification, privacy and security standards for AI use.
Everyone consults the security, privacy or data offices when unsure about data use with AI.
Students review the academic integrity policy or contact the named office with questions.
Researchers are directed to separate guidance on AI in research.
Instructors contact the named support offices with questions about AI use.
Everyone can find the list of approved AI tools and where to access them.
Anyone may contact the named office for questions or more information about AI.
